=================== map-frozen
card map-frozen  [decided]
A decided card is frozen. A change to it is an amend: a reopen and a decide in one step
why: Other cards depend on a decided card because of what it says. If its text could change without a reopen, those cards would not learn about the change. With this rule, an edit works the same way as an invalidation: both mark the next hop.

Frozen: the title, the why, the body, the depends_on links, and the parent. Free: options, sources, kill criterion state, and comments.

A change to a frozen field is a proposal (#al-diff-cli). Your ✓ amends the card: it reopens and decides it in one step, so the map never shows it open. The amend marks the next hop (#vi-prop).

The amend runs the decide facts (#werk-contract-facts) on the new version, so it can fail in two cases:
- The change removes a fact, for example the last depends_on link.
- The card was decided before a fact became required, for example a kill criterion. The amend waits until that fact is added.

An open or proto card is not frozen. It changes through a proposal and marks nothing, because no card can be decided on it.

       why: An amend is accepted the way #al-diff-cli stages and accepts an edit.
  -> depends_on      werk-contract-facts  A card needs four facts before it is decided
       why: An amend runs the decide facts that #werk-contract-facts lists.
  -> depends_on      vi-prop  A change marks the next hop only: direct dependents and direct children
       why: An amend is a change, so it marks the next hop as #vi-prop sets.
  <- alternative_to  map-frozen:opt-review  An edit stays in place and flags each link reason for review
  <- alternative_to  map-frozen:opt-free  An edit to a decided card marks nothing

Options
  map-frozen:opt-review  An edit stays in place and flags each link reason for review
    why not: A second mark next to stale, with its own clear. One mechanism for every change is simpler to read and to check.
  map-frozen:opt-free  An edit to a decided card marks nothing
    why not: The cards that depend on it do not learn about the change, so their link reasons can describe text that is no longer on the card.

=================== werk-cli-edit
card werk-cli-edit  [decided]
`werk edit` sets who, `--no-basis` and `--unchallenged` on a card without recreating it
why: A card that fails the decide check needs one missing fact recorded. Edit is the one command that records it, so the fix never costs a new card.

```
werk edit <id> [--who you|me|prototype] [--no-basis] [--unchallenged]
```

- `--who` sets who decides the card.
- `--no-basis` records that the card needs no depends_on target and no decided parent (#werk-contract-facts).
- `--unchallenged` records that no option was weighed against a `you` card (#werk-contract-guess).
- Each flag is a record on the card. None is a default.
- The flags apply to an open card. The text of a decided card is frozen: a change to it is a proposal, not an edit (#map-frozen, #al-diff-cli).
- The text of a ghost is frozen too. Discard it and propose it again (#werk-propose-new).

  -> depends_on      werk-contract-facts  A card needs four facts before it is decided

  -> depends_on      map-frozen  A decided card is frozen. A change to it is an amend: a reopen and a decide in one step
       why: Edit refuses the frozen fields because #map-frozen makes a change to them a proposal.
  -> depends_on      werk-propose-new  A new card is a proposal too, not a direct append

=================== vi-prop
card vi-prop  [decided]
A change marks the next hop only: direct dependents and direct children
why: A reopen or an amend marks the cards that depend on the changed card directly, and its direct children. A review that leaves a card unchanged stops the mark there. A review that changes the card is a change too, so the mark moves one hop more.
subtree: 8 cards, 8 decided

```
  ┌───┐  depends_on  ┌───┐  depends_on  ┌───┐
  │ C │─────────────▶│ B │─────────────▶│ A │◀── reopen or amend
  └───┘              └───┘              └───┘
  marked only if     STALE
  B is amended
```

The mark is derived from the log and never written. A card is stale when a card it depends on, or its parent, changed after the link existed, and the card has no review since. A link made after the change carries no mark (#vi-prop-bornstale). A review ends in a confirm or an amend (#rederive-reason). A card whose basis is stale waits. It is not stale (#map-wait).

A reopen with reason postponed marks cards paused, not stale. The paused mark reaches every card downstream, at any distance (#pr-wf-paused). A paused card is never reviewed, so a pause that moved one hop would stop at the first card.

  -> depends_on      vi-edges  Four link types: refines, depends_on, supported_by, alternative_to
       why: Propagation walks the depends_on edge, which #vi-edges defines as the one edge type that carries staleness.
  -> supported_by    grokers  Grokers: write-t

card werk-contract-amend-scope-option-remove  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
A decided card's option is removed one at a time, and the removal keeps an option
why: Removing an option is the one change that can leave a decided card without a required fact, so an option must be removable on its own, and only while the card keeps another option.

A removal names an option of a card in the map and takes that option with its own evidence. The card stays. When the card is decided and the option is its last one while who is you with no waiver, the removal is refused and the card keeps the option. After a second option is added, the first can go. A ghost option is dropped by a discard, not a removal.

  -> refines         werk-contract-amend-scope  A change to a decided card cannot leave it missing a required fact
card werk-contract-waiver-reason  [decided]
A waiver of a contract fact needs a written reason
why: A waiver leaves a required fact empty on purpose. Without a written reason, a reader later cannot tell a deliberate waiver from a forgotten fact.

The decide check lets a card go without a basis, or without a weighed option, when the author waives that fact (#werk-contract-facts). Every escape hatch of a check leaves a written reason (#pr-gate), so a waiver does too.

- The basis waiver says why no decided card is a basis, for example that the card is the root of a tree.
- The option waiver says why no option was weighed against the card (#werk-contract-guess).
- A waiver with an empty reason is refused.
- The reason is stored with the waiver and prints wherever the card prints.
- Who decides is not waivable. A kill criterion that names no metric already carries its reason.

 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
A decided card is frozen in its words and links (#map-frozen). Who decides and a waiver of a fact are frozen in the same way. They are not words, but the decide check read them, and a change to them can change what the card means to the cards that stand on it. A change to either goes through a proposal. Its accept is an amend: the facts run again on the new version, and the next hop is marked (#vi-prop-amended).

The amend can fail in the two cases that #map-frozen names: the change removes a fact, or the card lacks a fact that became required after it was decided. A kill criterion, an option and a source stay free, so a missing fact can always be added first (#werk-contract-amend-scope). A waiver still needs its written reason (#werk-contract-waiver-reason).

Each card that goes stale ends in a confirm or an amend of its own (#rederive-reason). An amend there marks one more hop.

Example. Three cards:
- P is "We charge per seat". It is decided, and who decides is me.
- Q is "The invoice shows the seat count". It depends on P.
- R is "The seat limit counts per workspace". It is a child of P.

What happens:
1. Someone proposes that who decides on P becomes you, with the sentence "The pricing model needs Eryk's judgement." Nothing changes yet. P stays decided, and Q and R stay clear.
2. P has no weighed option and no unchallenged record, so the accept is refused and names what is missing. The option is added, which needs no amend. The accept runs again and passes.
3. P stays decided, now with who decides you. Q and R go stale, and their trace shows amended with that sentence.
4. Q is reviewed and confirmed. It clears. R is reviewed and amended, so the cards that depend on R go stale.
5. A change that leaves who decides and every waiver as they are marks nothing.

The map checks the four facts of a decided card whenever a change could leave one missing (#werk-contract-facts). The check cannot treat every change alike. A card decided before a fact became required lacks that fact already, and the change that adds it must go through.

- A change to the title, the why, the body, a depends_on link or the parent: the card must hold all four facts after the change (#map-frozen). A card decided before a fact became required waits for that fact at its next such change.
- Any other change, such as recording who decides, a waiver, a kill criterion, a link to a source or the removal of an option: refused only when it removes a fact the card had. So a missing fact can always be added.
- Removing a card that this card depends on is not a change to this card, so the check does not refuse it.

The code now follows the three accepted cards: `#werk-contract-amend-who`, `#map-frozen` and `#werk-contract-amend-scope`. The full suite passes (1131 tests, 0 failures) and `tsc --noEmit` prints no errors. Oxlint prints warnings that I did not check against the new code.

I did not run the rule against the live map or the browser ✓, so only the tests have exercised it.

- **Who decides and waivers change by proposal.**
  - A proposal can now carry a new who-decides value and the waivers.
  - `werk edit` refuses these on a decided card and names the proposal to use.
- **The accept is checked.**
  - Accepting a change to a decided card needs all four facts after the change. A fact that is missing stops the accept and says which one.
  - The ✓ in the map runs the same check as the command-line accept.
  - Unlinking the last `depends_on` link of a decided card is refused. Unlinking the last option is refused too.
- **The accept is an amend.**
  - The card stays decided. Its direct dependents and children go stale, and the trace says "amended".
  - If the amended card was stale, its own mark clears. The review metric counts it as a review that changed the card.
- **Words of a decided card.** `edit --body`, `edit --why` and `retitle` are refused on a decided card. Open cards still edit in place.

The check is a new module, `src/amend.ts`, so the command line and the server use one rule.
